name: Hemoglobin Lepore Beta-Thalassemia Major
aliases: Hemoglobin Lepore Syndrome with Beta-Thalassemia Major

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Hemoglobin Lepore Beta-Thalassemia Major

criteria.description: Identification of Hb Lepore fusion gene combined with beta-thalassemia mutations by molecular genetic testing
Presence of severe microcytic hypochromic anemia with hemoglobin levels typically below 7 g/dL
Hemoglobin electrophoresis showing elevated Hb Lepore variant and reduced or absent HbA
Clinical features consistent with beta-thalassemia major including pallor, hepatosplenomegaly, and growth retardation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Molecular genetic confirmation of Hb Lepore fusion gene with beta-thalassemia mutations plus clinical and hematological evidence of severe beta-thalassemia major
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of genetic, hematological, and clinical data.

searchTerms: severe small pale red blood cells
intense anemia with tiny red cells

pathognomonic.symptomName: Elevated Hb Lepore variant on hemoglobin electrophoresis
searchTerms: high levels of Hb Lepore variant
increased Hb Lepore on blood test

common.symptomName: Bone deformities due to marrow expansion
searchTerms: bone deformities due to increased marrow activity
abnormal bone shape from marrow growth
yellow skin from red blood cell breakdown

common.symptomName: Iron overload complications secondary to transfusions
searchTerms: excess iron due to repeated transfusions

occasional.symptomName: Cardiac arrhythmias related to iron overload
searchTerms: heart rhythm problems related to iron
gallstones caused by chronic red cell breakdown
low sex hormone levels from iron
hormone deficiency due to iron deposits
stroke from lack of brain oxygen
high blood sugar from iron complications

laboratory: Severe microcytic hypochromic anemia with low hemoglobin and hematocrit
Elevated Hb Lepore variant on hemoglobin electrophoresis
Elevated serum ferritin and transferrin saturation indicating iron overload
Elevated indirect bilirubin due to hemolysis
imaging: Bone marrow expansion with cortical thinning on X-ray
Cardiac MRI showing myocardial iron deposition
other: Growth delay and endocrine dysfunction secondary to iron overload

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of Hb Lepore fusion gene
Different hemoglobin electrophoresis pattern without Hb Lepore variant
Presence of HbE variant instead of Hb Lepore
Milder clinical phenotype in some cases

redFlags: Signs of iron overload such as cardiac dysfunction or endocrine abnormalities
